elaine (Docs): FYI CI linkcheck is failing for several localized pages, looks like snippet includes an explicit id that collides across locale copies. sam (Platform): ugh, seen that before with generated examples. can you paste the failing output? elaine (Docs): here — mkdocs-linkcheck output from last run: ``` ERROR: Broken anchor on /docs/zh/guide/deploy/#example-start referenced from /docs/zh/guide/deploy/ (line 42) ERROR: Duplicate id 'example-start' in /docs/zh/guide/deploy/ and /docs/en/guide/deploy/ caused by injected snippet: examples/snippets/deploy.md ``` mike (Infra): that duplicate id across locales is the issue — our output pipeline copies en -> zh then runs include processing, so any explicit `id="..."` in snippets will duplicate. elaine (Docs): snippet looks like this: ```
```bash ./deploy --env=prod ```
``` jen (Eng): yep, raw HTML wrappers showing up in snippets. Markdown include just pastes them into each localized page. quick fixes: 1) strip wrapper ids during snippet inclusion; 2) scope ids by locale (e.g., prefix with lang code); or 3) prefer anchorless snippets and use ad-hoc header ids in page. sam (Platform): option 1 seems safest and smallest. we can add a sanitizer step in the docs pipeline that removes `id="..."` attributes from top-level snippet wrappers. i'll volunteer to PR. @mike any infra gotchas? :eyes: mike (Infra): should be fine. make it opt-in via a mkdocs plugin flag so we can toggle if needed. also add a warning log when an id is stripped so we can track regressions. elaine (Docs): thanks. i'll audit snippets for any places that relied on those wrapper ids (search for `id=\"example-`). only saw ~6 occurrences. sam (Platform): created draft branch `docs/sanitize-snippet-ids` and opened PR #4321 — short patch adds `strip_snippet_ids` config and a warning emited via the plugin. docs-ci-bot: CI pipeline started for PR #4321 (mkdocs-build, linkcheck). mike (Infra): ping when linkcheck passes, will flip the flag on staging pipeline. jen (Eng): small nit — instead of raw `div` wrappers consider using fenced HTML comments that are non-rendering, e.g. `` then transform into localized unique anchors if truly needed. less likely to break linkcheck. elaine (Docs): good idea — i'll drop a follow-up ticket to standardize snippet anchors and update the contributor guide. sam (Platform): CI green on PR #4321: build and linkcheck passed on staging. :tada: I'll merge and roll out to prod docs pipeline tomorrow morning with the flag enabled. elaine (Docs): thanks everyone — i'll close out the small snippet PRs and open an umbrella issue for contributor guidance. :thumbsup:
